title: So there is no reason to deny God this knowledge without a predetermining decree; the objections strike absolute foreknowledge too
source_text: LXIII. Nihil ergo video cur negemus Deo scientiam eorum quae libere futura essent sub certa conditione, quanquam in conditione ista non includatur decretum de causa libera ad hoc vel illud praedeterminanda. Et si quae argumenta scientiam istam videntur evertere, ut quod capi non potest qua ratione Deus infallibiliter cognoscat futurum esse quod posset non esse, pugnant illa quoque cum praescientia contingentium quae sunt absolute futura; quam tamen in Deo dari verbum Dei ponit extra omne dubium.
pass_a_gloss: LXIII. I see nothing therefore why we should deny to God the knowledge of those things which would be freely future under a certain condition, although in that condition there be not included a decree concerning predetermining the free cause to this or that. And if any arguments seem to overturn that knowledge, as that it cannot be grasped by what reason God infallibly knows that to be future which could not be, those also fight against the foreknowledge of contingents which are absolutely future; which yet the word of God puts beyond all doubt to be in God.
pass_b_english: I therefore see no reason to deny God knowledge of what would freely happen under a certain condition, even though the condition does not include a decree predetermining the free cause to this or that.

If any arguments seem to overthrow that knowledge, for instance that it cannot be grasped how God infallibly knows something to be future that could fail to be, those arguments also conflict with the foreknowledge of contingents that are absolutely future, and God's word puts it beyond all doubt that God has that foreknowledge.
